---
title: "Probability Vectors — Store Every Possibility in One Column"
description: "A compact linear-algebra lesson with mathematical definitions, real values and reasoning."
---

## Start with a question

A machine can be in two states: working or broken. How do you describe uncertainty about which one it is?

## Understand the central idea

A probability vector lists all mutually exclusive outcome probabilities, each nonnegative and adding to one.

## Express it with mathematics

$$
\mathbf p=\begin{bmatrix}0.8\\0.2\end{bmatrix},\qquad\sum_i p_i=1
$$

**Every symbol explained:** p is a vector of probabilities; p_i is the probability of outcome i; Σ means add probabilities across all possible mutually exclusive states; 1 represents certainty that one state occurs.

**Substitute real numbers:** The machine works with probability 0.8=80% and is broken with probability 0.2=20%. The sum 0.8+0.2=1. If a proposed vector were (0.8,0.5), it would total 1.3 and could not describe just these two exhaustive states.

## Why this works

A probability distribution acts like weights on a collection of outcomes. Storing the weights in a vector lets matrices describe how probabilities shift over time.

## What can go wrong?

Probabilities are not the same as amplitudes in quantum mechanics. The squared magnitude of quantum amplitude, not its raw value, gives measurement probability.

## Your turn

Write the two-state vector when the machine works 95% of the time.
